correctness.rationale: For real planar SPD A, the bilinear form is the quadratic form of the symmetric Jordan product with SᵀS. It has positive diagonal almost surely in the eigenbasis and has a negative direction exactly when the squared column cosine exceeds 4κ/(κ+1)². Gaussian decomposition into parallel and perpendicular parts gives independent χ²_1 and χ²_(k−1) and the asserted beta tail. For a fixed v the normalized outputs are g and c(v)g+√(1−c(v)²)h with g,h independent standard Gaussian columns. Conditioning on g gives a one-sided normal tail mixed by ||g||²∼χ²_k and yields the asserted half-beta law, including k=1 and zero risk for c(v)=1. Differentiation gives the attainable minimum cosine at high-mode squared weight 1/(κ+1). The row shift is exact. The ratio limit follows from kR² converging to χ²_1 as k grows, the small-threshold argument when k is bounded and κ grows, and E R²=1/k for the strongly oversampled case. The iff follows by subsequence extraction. Independent low-row angular and Gaussian-conditioning checks passed (/workspace/independent_checks.py). In the scope note, zero probability of equality applies to a prescribed v or to the singular determinant threshold, not to existence of a sketch-adaptive null vector: an indefinite form has such null directions. The proof uses the determinant boundary and the main strict-negativity formulas are unaffected. No claim about Ritz eigenvalues of an entire two-dimensional pencil was verified.

evidence: The fixed-pair law is half the beta tail in complementary cosine-squared. Minimizing c(v)²=(1+(κ−1)t)²/(1+(κ²−1)t) gives 4κ/(κ+1)² by setting t=1/(κ+1); this is the standard sharp SPD angle extremum.

Replacing k by k−1 in the resulting fixed-vector beta law makes its beta parameters identical to those of the adaptive law, with factor two. For κ→∞ the finite positive ratio limit is in the prior proof; β-tail monotonicity in the row parameter sandwiches the zero and infinite ratio cases by arbitrarily small or large fixed positive ratios.

originality.rationale: Indexed record 82e6f28b1c80 states the same uniform law in complement form on an arbitrary fixed invariant two-eigenvector plane, the same critical normal profile, and the sharper fixed-tolerance row-budget statement. Scaling Gaussian entries by √k does not affect signs. For the precommitted direction, Kabán–Durrant's exact fixed-pair sign-flip formula applies directly to (v,Av). It is monotone in their cosine, so evaluating it at the minimum of the one-variable angle expression yields the frozen worst-fixed law, including k=1. Once these two covered formulas are written in beta form, the one-row bridge is a substitution, and its fixed-vector limits follow from the uniform law. This is substantial direct coverage plus immediate consequences, not a negative-search verdict.

value.rationale: The adaptive versus precommitted distinction is relevant for positivity of one-dimensional sketched projections. But the adaptive risk and sharp scale were already given, the precommitted maximum is obtained by the standard fixed-pair probability and an elementary attained angle minimum, and the row shift is direct beta-parameter matching. The frozen result is a useful juxtaposition, not a distinct scientific finding at the stated bar.
